episodes.173113: Scattered thunderstorms formed during the heat of the day along a cold front as it sagged into southeast Missouri. The storms formed within a corridor of 1000 to 1500 J/kg mixed-layer capes across the Ozarks into extreme western Tennessee. As thunderstorms spread southeast within this moderately unstable air mass, there was sufficient wind shear to support a few organized storm cells that produced large hail.
episodes.173492: Strong to severe storms affected areas along and south of Highway 60 from the afternoon of the 23rd to the early morning of the 25th. The strongest storms developed during the afternoon of the 24th along Highway 60, and produced damaging wind gusts over 60 mph. Rainfall accumulations over two inches occurred over portions of south central Missouri from Mansfield to Winona.
episodes.174212: An abundance of moisture (PWAT 1.5+) and moderate to high instability (MLCAPE of 1000-2000 J/KG) led to the development of terrain and diurnally induced thunderstorm activity. Thunderstorms first began to develop across portions of southwestern Arizona during the early afternoon hours and thereafter, additional storm development occurred across the higher terrain east of Phoenix. Outflow from storms, particularly across the higher terrain east of Phoenix led to the development of more storms across portions of the Phoenix metro, particularly in the area between Chandler and Queen Creek.
episodes.174213: An abundance of moisture (PWAT 1.5+) and moderate to high instability (MLCAPE of 1000-2000 J/KG) led to the development of terrain and diurnally induced thunderstorm activity across portions of southwest Arizona during the afternoon hours. Some of this activity spread westward across the Lower Colorado River Valley towards extreme eastern Riverside County, where a slowing moving thunderstorm led to flash flooding and debris flow along Highway 95 north of Blythe.
episodes.174588: Isolated thunderstorms moved east across southeast Arizona during the late afternoon and evening. One storm produced large hail in Oracle.

events.narrative: A low-water crossing along Highway 72 just northwest of Bouse was impassible due to flooding. No damages or injuries were reported.
Water, rocks, and debris were reported across Hwy 95 north of Blythe. No injuries were reported.
A 63 mph wind gust was measured at the Chandler Municipal Airport.
A few large limbs were reported down along a rural county road.
Quarter-size hail was reported just west of Ellsinore. Half-dollar size hail broke a house window in Ellsinore.
